"After we'd recorded it, I looked at the tape box and didn't even notice that I'd changed the title. For those of you who don't know, I teach a few students at a private Irish pub on Thursday nights. Later in the evening, after the ladies are done with their Irish Dance class, I lead everyone in pub songs. I wrote a song about it with one of my students. I'm not thrilled with the vox mix on this, so I'll definitely spend more time on the mix later, but I was in a hurry to get a mixdown tonight. I currently have one student and she appears really dedicated. I'd thought about sending her out for lessons, but doing it to impress me seems to give her extra motivation. I didn't really want a student, but here we are. She keeps asking me when I'll teach her a song. I tell her I'll teach her one in a year or two. ;-)

Right now, I have her only doing drills. That's it. She's brand new and I want her to start with good habits and proper form. She doesn't know the price but I let her have a Yamaha GC32. I even gave her one of my old foot stools, so she's playing with proper classical form. She has learned a number of chords and throws them together well enough for a second month student.

If I skip a few steps, she'll be ready in a decade. I've never taught anyone to play classical guitar before. I've never had a complete beginner before. It's actually easier with a complete beginner. I don't have to fix previously learned form issues, correct silly notions, etc...

In all seriousness, she's coming along nicely. I'm absolutely enjoying myself. The youngest seems a little interested in percussion but he's outside too much to practice. I have a kit in the garage that I might put new heads on, tune, and give it to him. Man, I hate tuning drums.

Side note: I find it funny how well we actually stay on topic. Mosts posts are, in fact, related to music. It doesn't completely devolve into things like what we had for dinner.

I've got three students left out of four... I lost the most apt student due to her young age. She's young (30), and still at a point in her life where she has a million things going on, and guitar isn't a priority. She still does play a mean bodhran on pub nights, though! She's also part of the small 'Scully's Pub Ensemble' that we put together to play a few holiday events and such. Two of my remaining students are 60 and 75 respectively. 60 works his butt off. He practices constantly. Guitar isn't easy for him, and he really, really works hard at it. The other guys may be more naturally talented, but their lack of practice means that they aren't progressing, while 60 is!

I have just the one. I taught my son rock guitar, which is very different to learn. She's a mere 15 years old and completely disregards her peers.

Given that she was previously poor, she's not addicted to her phone, Facebook, twitter, or anything like that. She's putting in one to two hours of practice, most days. I'm very excited to see where this goes. It's a very eager brain and she wants very much to impress. She's also working with the missus to learn sound and lights. One of the band members is qualified and has been showing the two of them. She just kept watching and asking questions.

Next Thursday night, strange I know, is my next gig. I spoke about it in the thread. I have permission to keep her out of school on Friday, as they're not doing anything that day and she can turn in her books on Monday. So, she's going to work that show with us.

Getting a young AND dedicated mind is why I agreed.
